source.note: The recovered prototype combines family profiles, parent approvals, tasks, rewards, messages, streaks and learning with simulated token-price, wallet-address and staking language. LarriVerse preserves the family system while replacing the pretend-finance layer. Phase 17 keeps learning and browsing open while focusing Parent Mode on assigning chores, approving earned Family KC, and approving reward redemptions.

boundaries.pinNote: The parent PIN is a convenience lock on this browser, not strong account security.

lessons.title: Earn before spending
lessons.summary: Family KC grows through completed learning and parent-approved chores before rewards are redeemed.

questions.prompt: Which action can add Family KC to the ledger?
options: A parent approves a completed chore
questions.explanation: Approved chores can earn Family KC.

questions.prompt: What happens after an explorer marks an assigned chore done?
options: It is sent for parent approval
questions.explanation: Chores wait in the private parent approval queue.

questions.prompt: Why is the ledger useful?
options: It shows earned and redeemed Family KC
questions.explanation: The ledger records fictional family rewards and redemptions.

questions.prompt: Who can assign chores to an explorer?
questions.explanation: Parent Mode is used to assign chores on this device.

questions.prompt: What is true about Family KC?
questions.explanation: Family KC is fictional and has no cash value.

questions.prompt: Which learning action is open without Parent Mode?
questions.explanation: Learning rounds are open to explorers without unlocking Parent Mode.

lessons.title: Needs and wants
lessons.summary: Needs keep daily life safe and working; wants are extras that can usually wait.

questions.prompt: Which is usually a need?
questions.explanation: Safe food is a basic need.

questions.prompt: Which item is a need on a cold winter day?
questions.explanation: A warm coat helps protect the body from cold weather.

questions.prompt: Which is usually a want?
questions.explanation: A special toy is usually an extra rather than a basic need.

questions.prompt: What is a smart first step when KC is limited?
questions.explanation: Planning starts by handling needs before extras.

questions.prompt: Why can a want wait?
options: It is an extra, not an immediate necessity
questions.explanation: Wants are extras that can often be saved for.

questions.prompt: Which plan shows careful thinking?
options: Save for an extra after important needs are covered
questions.explanation: Good planning protects needs and saves toward wants.

lessons.title: Saving for a goal
lessons.summary: A larger reward may take several smaller earning steps and patient choices.

questions.prompt: What helps reach a 36 KC goal?
questions.explanation: Keeping part of each reward helps a balance grow.

questions.prompt: You have 18 KC and earn 9 KC. What is the new balance?
questions.explanation: Eighteen plus nine equals 27.

questions.prompt: You have 24 KC and your goal is 36 KC. How much more is needed?
questions.explanation: Thirty-six minus twenty-four equals 12.

questions.prompt: Which goal is easiest to follow?
options: Save 6 KC from each approved chore until reaching 36 KC
questions.explanation: A specific step-by-step goal is easier to track.

questions.prompt: What should you do before requesting a reward?
options: Compare your balance with its KC cost
questions.explanation: The app uses only the fictional balance and reward cost.

questions.prompt: What can patience do for a bigger goal?
options: Give time for several earnings to add up
questions.explanation: Several small earnings can build toward a larger family reward.

lessons.title: Read the ledger
lessons.summary: Earn entries add to the balance and approved redemption entries subtract from it.

questions.prompt: What does a positive ledger entry mean?
questions.explanation: Positive entries add fictional Family KC.

questions.prompt: What does a negative ledger entry mean here?
questions.explanation: Negative entries show an approved family reward redemption.

questions.prompt: A balance is 30 KC and 9 KC is redeemed. What remains?
questions.explanation: Thirty minus nine equals 21.

questions.prompt: Why does each entry include a label?
options: To explain what was earned or redeemed
questions.explanation: Labels make the family history easier to understand.

questions.prompt: Where is the KidsCoin ledger stored?
options: In this browser on this device
questions.explanation: The ledger stays in this browser's local storage.

questions.prompt: Which entry should be checked if a balance changed?
questions.explanation: The ledger record explains each local balance change.

lessons.title: Plan a reward
lessons.summary: Compare the balance with the reward cost, then send a request for a parent decision.

questions.prompt: You have 18 KC and a reward costs 27 KC. What is true?
options: You can pay cash in the app
questions.explanation: Twenty-seven minus eighteen equals 9.

questions.prompt: What happens when an explorer requests a reward?
options: KC is sent to a stranger
questions.explanation: Reward requests go to the private parent queue.

questions.prompt: When is KC deducted for a reward?
questions.explanation: Family KC is deducted only after approval.

questions.prompt: Which reward is easier to reach first?
options: A 27 KC reward instead of a 72 KC reward
A reward with no cost shown
questions.explanation: A lower KC cost requires fewer earning steps.

questions.prompt: Who decides whether the timing of a reward works?
questions.explanation: Parents or caregivers make the final family decision.

questions.prompt: What is a good reward plan?
options: Name the goal, check the cost, and save toward it
questions.explanation: A clear goal and cost make saving easier.

lessons.title: Family KC is pretend
lessons.summary: Family KC has no cash value, never leaves this browser, and is only for parent-approved family rewards.

questions.prompt: What can Family KC be used for?
questions.explanation: Family KC is only for the private family reward system.

questions.prompt: Can Family KC be exchanged for cash?
questions.explanation: Family KC has no cash value.

questions.prompt: Does KidsCoin create a public child account?
questions.explanation: Profiles are device-local and not public accounts.

questions.prompt: Should an explorer share the parent PIN?
questions.explanation: The parent PIN should stay within the family.

questions.prompt: Does the app use blockchain or staking?
questions.explanation: The finance and crypto systems are intentionally excluded.

questions.prompt: What leaves the browser when a family note is sent?
options: Nothing; the note stays on this device
The note is sold to advertisers
questions.explanation: Family notes stay inside this browser.
